item.title: 重读自由软件宣言：计算在谁的机器上
On Rereading
item.description: The first time through a book you read to find out what happens. Every time after that, you read to find out who you were.

item.title: Notes, August
item.description: Four things from a month of not writing much: a misprint, a cheap notebook, a quiet chapter, and a letter that took nine days.

item.title: A Due Date from 1987
item.description: A secondhand copy of Middlemarch still has its library card in the back. Someone renewed it four times.

item.title: The Unhurried Newsletter
item.description: A note on writing to a schedule you set yourself, and why the best newsletters read like letters, not broadcasts.

item.title: Footnotes Are a Form of Honesty
item.description: The footnote lets a writer admit doubt, digress, and cite a source without breaking the sentence that needed to stay clean.

item.title: The Commonplace Book, Revisited
item.description: Before there were note-taking apps there were commonplace books, and the old method still beats most of the new ones.

item.title: A Typography Sampler
item.description: One essay, deliberately overloaded: headings, quotes, footnotes, lists, a table, and some code, in service of a single argument.

item.title: Marginalia and Other Small Rebellions
item.description: In praise of writing in books, underlining badly, and arguing with authors who cannot argue back.

item.title: A Short History of the Serif
item.description: Why letters grew little feet, and what four centuries of stonecutters, scribes, and engineers did with them.

item.title: On the Pleasure of Slow Reading
item.description: A case for reading fewer books more slowly, on the theory that speed was never the point of a sentence.
